newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Arab petrochemicals output to rise 3.6 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Arab petrochemicals output to rise 3.6 mln tonnes.

text.p: Total Arab petrochemicals output could rise by 3.6 million tonnes a year from 46 projects being studied or under construction, an OAPEC expert said on Monday.

But "Despite the large steps made in the petrochemicals industry in Arab states during the past 20 years, it is still below the aspired level" in countries which control 65 percent of global proven oil reserves and 12 percent of the world's natural gas reserves, al-Tayeb Wanadah told a seminar.
He put total Arab output of petrochemicals at 16 million tonnes a year from 152 projects mainly in Gulf Arab states.
Wanadah was addressing an oil and gas seminar hosted by the 11-nation Organisation of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries (OAPEC) at its Kuwait headquarters.

His figures showed that 31.3 percent of total Arab output of petrochemicals was in the form of olefins and basic aromatics, 26.5 percent intermediate petrochemicals, 21.6 percent finished products and 20.6 percent methanol.

Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil producer and exporter, produces 74.2 percent of the total Arab output of 3.3 million tonnes a year of ethylene. The kingdom has three such plants while Libya, Qatar, Iraq and Algeria each have one project.
Kuwait's ethylene plant, with a 650,000 tonne a year production capacity, is due to come onstream later this year while Egypt is studying a 150,000-tonne project, Wanadah's study showed.
Saudi Arabia also leads the list of Arab methanol producers with 62.6 percent of the total output of three million tonnes a year. Libya accounts for 21 percent followed by Bahrain's 12.6.
Qatar is due to start construction this year of a project with a production capacity of 550,000 tonnes a year of methanol.

Some 68 percent of total Arab production of widely used plastics of 2.2 million tonnes a year comes from Saudi Arabia which spent huge funds in the past 20 years, including $14 billion on a gas collection system, developing an advanced petrochemicals industry.
